findings.title: Skip/respawn/finish does not cancel the running camera tween, so it fights the restored Custom camera for up to 5.5 s
findings.explanation: shot() starts a TweenService tween on Camera.CFrame (3-5.5 s) and keeps no reference to it. Finish() bumps the token, sets CameraType Custom and the Humanoid subject, but never cancels the tween. Roblox's camera controller takes its look direction from camera.CFrame every frame, so the leftover tween keeps forcing the view along its path (shot 1 ends looking almost straight up at the crown). It also overrides the player's own camera rotation until the tween ends. This shows on menu-replay skips and on respawns. A23-9 asks for an exact camera restore and warns about the earlier camera-restore bug.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the tween in state.CamTween. Cancel the previous tween in shot() before starting a new one, and in Finish() before setting CameraType Custom. Optionally save camera.CFrame in Play(true) and set it back on Finish so a replay returns to the old view.
findings.verifier_note: Re-read at 14:19 with no change. Intro.luau:189-190 starts a camera.CFrame tween and keeps no reference to it. Finish() (Intro.luau:260-283) changes the CameraType to Custom and sets the subject, but never cancels that tween. The default camera takes its direction from camera.CFrame every frame; CameraFollow.luau relies on the same fact (its comment says 'Only the direction is changed; Roblox computes the subject position, distance and collision next'). So the leftover tween (3 to 5.5 s) keeps steering or fighting the player's view after a skip, a respawn or the end of a replay. CameraFollow restores only the subject; nothing in the code cancels tweens. Fix: keep the tween in state, call :Cancel() in shot() before starting a new one and in Finish() before switching to Custom. Optionally save the camera CFrame before a replay and put it back afterwards.

findings.verifier_note: Intro.luau:298-301 binds Space, Return, ButtonA and ButtonB at priority 3000, and the first Begin press calls Finish(). On the first viewing Finish() then sends IntroSeen (Intro.luau:276-277), which is saved for good. Space and pad A are the jump keys, and movement is disabled during the opening, so a reflexive jump press ends it. A23-9 does require a PC skip key, so this is a choice of key, not a missing feature. Suggest ignoring skip keys for about 1.5 s after Play(), or using Enter plus the button and pad B only, and updating the '(Space)' hint.

findings.title: Finish() can yield on Net.Get before state.Done/Refresh, which would hide the faction cards for good
findings.explanation: On the client, Net.Get uses WaitForChild with no timeout. If the IntroSeen remote is missing (for example a Studio session where the server copy of Net was not re-synced), Finish waits forever before state.Done = true and FactionPicker.Refresh. Intro.Blocking() then stays true, so FactionPicker.IsOpen() stays false and the new player is stuck with no cards and no HUD. This should not happen in production, where both sides share Net.
findings.suggested_fix: Set state.Done = true and call FactionPicker.Refresh/FlushBanners before reporting. Send the remote inside task.spawn, or look it up with FindFirstChild instead of waiting.
findings.verifier_note: The failure path cannot happen. Net is a single shared ModuleScript (ReplicatedStorage/Shared/Net.luau), so there is no separate server copy that could fall out of sync. Net.CreateAll creates every Net.Names entry, including "IntroSeen" (Net.luau:12), when the server starts. The client's WaitForChild in Net.Get (Net.luau:60-62) therefore returns at once, more than 15 s after DataLoaded. If the remote were missing, every remote would be missing and the game would be broken anyway. Setting state.Done before the FireServer call is only a harmless tidy-up.

findings.explanation: A23-3 asks for the toast only once. hadNextGoal is per session, not saved. Either way, the GuideDone toast fires again once the goal is met. A23-3 only says to toast once when the row disappears, so whether a repeat after rebirth is acceptable is for the user to decide. Rejoining does not repeat the toast.

findings.title: Server-wide goose rare-reward alert is sent as an 'info' toast, so it is not held during the opening or pickers
findings.explanation: A23-9/A23-3 defer server-wide goose/kaiju/war/bounty alerts while the opening or selection screens are open, but only the 'announce' kind is held. The goose rare-reward message to all players (and GrudgeAvengedAll, also 'info') still shows as a toast during the opening and the first mission.
findings.suggested_fix: Send these NotifyAll messages with the 'announce' kind (or a kind the client holds), or hold toasts from NotifyAll while UIKit.ShouldHoldBanners() is true.
findings.verifier_note: GooseService.luau:467 sends RareAnnounce to everyone with "info" (this was already the case at HEAD), and GrudgeService.luau:188 sends GrudgeAvengedAll with "info". UIKit.luau:1872 holds only payloads of kind "announce", so these two still show as toasts during the opening and the pickers. The other server-wide alerts are held correctly: the Kaiju, War, Bounty, MostWanted and Rebirth NotifyAll calls take the default kind "announce" (Net.luau:73-75). Fix: send these two with "announce", or have toasts that arrived through NotifyAll go through ShouldHoldBanners.

missed: low | UIKit.luau:1832-1841 ShouldHoldBanners() holds banners only when 'TutorialStep == 0' or Intro.IsOpen(). It never checks FactionPicker.IsOpen or ClassPicker.IsOpen, although A23-9 also asks to hold alerts while the selection screens are open. New players are covered because their TutorialStep is 0. Two groups are not: a returning player with Faction 'None' and TutorialStep 99 (an old save, or a corrupted faction reset to None at FactionService.luau:395), and a v1-migrated player with ClassChosen=false (DataService.luau:112). For them, goose, kaiju, war and bounty banners show over the pickers. Fix: add the two picker IsOpen checks to ShouldHoldBanners, and refresh the picker state when it closes.

low | Intro.luau:321-323 with 328-333: the server loads the first character only after setting DataLoaded (PlayerService.luau:480-484). Intro.Start waits at most 10 s for HumanoidRootPart and then plays anyway from a fallback position. If the character arrives later, the CharacterAdded handler calls Finish() right away. Because state.Replay is false, Finish also sends IntroSeen, so the new player loses the opening permanently after about a second. Fix: in Intro.Start, do not play until a character exists, falling back to the cards; or report IntroSeen only for a real skip or end, not for a respawn-triggered Finish.
